status: Substantive source reviewed; independent build, runtime and equivalence untested
notes: m68 directly loads 68000 CP/M-68K .68K, Linux-style ELF and Motorola hex programs. The repository contains a substantial custom C++ 68000 interpreter, executable loaders and host OS-service implementations. README and cpm/m.sh show original Digital Research compiler/assembler/linker stages being invoked through m68; MT Pascal, CB68 BASIC, DDT, SVS tools and Forth examples are documented uses of this one runner. Inspected default-branch head: 45b0c7378c7adc4433141d33cf5dd119b9cca612. A tooling emulator and partial OS-API reimplementation, not recovered source for the guest compilers. load_cpm68k reads the 0x601a executable header, creates a basepage and relocates text/data/BSS; trap 2 implements BDOS and trap 3 BIOS, with host fopen/fread-backed files. Trap 0 handles supported Linux-style services and trap 15 Fondse-style calls. The direct-run path constructs runtime state without booting CP/M or loading a ROM. 68000 is explicit in README, m68000.cxx and the loaders. CP/M-68K is retained under canonical CP/M; Linux here means the supported m68k ELF/syscall convention, not every Linux executable. README requires its newlib startup/BSP stubs for sample applications, and source explicitly limits BDOS to calls used by tested compiler families. Addresses are not constrained to physical 68000 24-bit behavior. Nested 6502/Z80/x86 interpreters running as guests do not expand m68 itself into those guest ISAs. README explicitly reports host tests on AMD64 Windows/Ubuntu, ARM64 Raspberry Pi OS/Ubuntu/macOS, ARM32 Raspberry Pi 4 and RISC-V64 Debian. Canonical target labels preserve x86-64, ARM64, ARM and RISC-V. c_tests/mm68.sh also targets -mcpu=68000 with m68k-elf-gcc to run m68 recursively in an existing m68 instance; target_cpu=m68000 refers to that distinct emulated-runtime output, not an asserted physical CP/M host port or arbitrary Linux/m68k compatibility. MSVC and g++ release scripts compile the emulator; the Linux recipe links statically and the macOS recipe sets signed-char behavior. The nested 68000 build uses m68k-elf-gcc, explicit 68000 options and newlib BSP support. Guest cross-compiler construction is separate: README reports GCC 8.2 build difficulties on macOS/Pi 5 and a GCC13 guest-test issue. These are maintainer claims, not independent failures here.
